data.title: Alibaba revenue tops estimates as AI cloud growth offsets e-commerce weakness
data.description:
Alibaba Group’s (BABA) revenue for the second quarter topped expectations, driven by strong growth in its AI cloud business, although adjusted net income and earnings per American depositary share fell short of estimates as the company continued to ramp up investment in technology infrastructure.

Revenue rose 10% year over year to 271.52 billion yuan ($40.5 billion), compared with the consensus of 270.53 billion yuan, as per data compiled by Bloomberg. 

Non-GAAP net income increased 92% to 19.91 billion yuan, missing the 26.61 billion yuan estimate. Adjusted earnings per ADS rose 86% to 8.10 yuan, below expectations of 10.75 yuan. Adjusted EBITDA climbed to 46.06 billion yuan, beating the 39.9 billion yuan consensus.

AI Cloud and Compute Services revenue jumped 53% to 60.97 billion yuan, ahead of the 59.77 billion yuan estimate. Revenue from external customers increased 64%, while recurring revenue from external customers rose 67%, reflecting greater adoption of AI-related products. Revenue from AI Labs and Applications grew 51% to 4.44 billion yuan, also above expectations.

Alibaba (BABA) E-commerce Group revenue edged up 2% to 197.24 billion yuan, slightly below the 197.53 billion yuan estimate. China e-commerce revenue declined 5%, while China Quick Commerce revenue increased 22%.

The company’s adjusted EBITA rose 260% to 32.64 billion yuan, supported by improved results in its cloud and quick-commerce businesses and operating efficiencies. However, free cash flow was an outflow of 34.47 billion yuan, wider than the 21.84 billion yuan outflow a year earlier, as higher cloud infrastructure spending offset improvements elsewhere.

Capital expenditure increased 60% to 50.48 billion yuan. Alibaba (BABA) said it would continue investing in AI capabilities while focusing on returns on invested capital and targeting positive free cash flow.

Seeking Alpha analyst Geneva Investor said Alibaba’s “AI CapEx, AI Labs losses, and quick commerce spending” continued to weigh on per-share earnings and cash flow, despite strong cloud growth. The analyst maintained a Sell view, saying a recovery in customer management revenue and positive free cash flow “in the same quarter” were needed to change the outlook.

Shares edged down 2.1% in the premarket trading on Thursday and are down 42.4% year to date, significantly underperforming the broader market index, which has gained around 7% during the same period.

data.title: The Amazon Kindle begins its 20th year of upending the bookstore model
data.description:
Amazon (AMZN) gave a makeover of its Kindle line as the e-reader product begins its 20th year as an alternative to books. The base Kindle, Paperwhite, and Colorsoft are redesigned with flush displays, plastic or aluminum casings, and thinner, lighter bodies. The entry-level Kindle is advertised as 30% faster at opening books than the 2024 model, and the Colorsoft has an improved display with better clarity and uniformity. Amazon (AMZN) also introduced the Kindle Click, a $34.99 Bluetooth page-turning remote, along with Kids editions of the three models. 

Looking back, the first Kindle sold out in about five and a half hours in 2007. It was a clunky, angular device with a physical keyboard and a 6-inch E Ink screen, priced at $399. What set it apart was its built-in free wireless connection, called Whispernet, which let readers buy and download a book from anywhere without a computer. Amazon (AMZN) had also lined up around 90K titles at launch, which was much more than other e-readers at the time.

Over the years the line kept evolving. The Kindle DX brought a larger screen, later models dropped the keyboard for touch, and the Paperwhite added a built-in light in 2012. Waterproofing, USB-C charging, the Scribe for handwritten notes, and the Colorsoft, Amazon's (AMZN) first color E Ink Kindle, followed. Of course, the Kindle’s importance to the industry was that it turned e-books from a niche curiosity into a mainstream format, pushed publishers to digitize their catalogs, and helped spawn self-publishing through Kindle Direct Publishing, which gave independent authors a path to readers without a traditional publisher.

data.title: Vail Resorts says it has the right board and strategy in place
data.description:
Vail Resorts (MTN) published a presentation that made the case that shareholders should retain the current board because it has already recognized performance problems, changed leadership, and begun implementing a credible growth strategy. The ongoing proxy contest was described as a choice between maintaining momentum and unnecessary disruption. Vail (MTN) noted that activist investor Oasis largely agrees with its strategic direction and offers neither a superior plan nor better-qualified directors.

The defense of the board attributed much of the share price weakness to factors such as post-pandemic valuation compression, normalized travel demand, and exceptionally poor snowfall. The board called Rob Katz’s May 2025 return as CEO a decisive corrective action, highlighting approximately twelvefold total shareholder returns during his previous tenure. It also emphasizes the hiring of former Lululemon (LULU) executive Celeste Burgoyne as chief revenue officer and three director additions since 2024, arguing that leadership and governance changes began before the proxy contest.

Vail (MTN) also pointed to stronger pass-sales trends following marketing changes, lift-ticket visitation outperforming the industry by three percentage points in FY26, and record guest satisfaction and employee engagement. Looking ahead, the company's future plan shifts the growth engine from expanding resort access toward increasing guest loyalty, spending, and lifetime value across Vail's (MTB) 42-resort network. Its "Epic Experience" strategy combines personalized engagement through the My Epic app, premium equipment access through My Epic Gear, digitized ski-school services, premium lessons, better dining, and stronger frontline service. 

The initiatives also include cost discipline. Vail (MTN) expects $105M in savings from its original efficiency program, plus another $30M by fiscal 2028. For fiscal years 2028–2030, it targets long-term growth of 3% to 5% in revenue, 5% to 7% in resort reported EBITDA, and 7% to 9% in adjusted free cash flow, excluding acquisitions and new business opportunities. 

Shares of Vail Resorts (MTN) are up 17.9% on a year-to-date basis.

data.title: Torex Resources renews share buyback plan
data.description:
Torex Resources (TXR) said it received approval from the Toronto Stock Exchange to renew its normal course issuer bid.

Under the renewed bid, the company is authorized to repurchase up to 7,176,403 common shares, representing approximately 10% of its public float as of November 11, 2026. The program will run from November 23, 2026, through November 22, 2027.

As of November 11, 2026, Torex had 90,251,272 common shares issued and outstanding, with a public float of 71,764,036 shares.

Under its existing NCIB, which commenced on November 21, 2025, and expires on November 20, 2026, Torex received approval to repurchase up to 8,133,430 common shares.

As of November 11, 2026, the company had repurchased 6,260,801 common shares through the TSX at a volume-weighted average price of approximately C$68.08 per share, excluding commissions.

data.title: Pennsylvania confirms eighth measles-linked death this year
data.description:
Pennsylvania health officials have confirmed the state's eighth measles-associated death this year, a day after the U.S. officially lost its measles elimination status that was in place since 2000.

The Pennsylvania Department of Health on Wednesday said an unvaccinated resident of Clinton County tested positive for measles and died. 

Pennsylvania has been remains the hardest hit by the ongoing measles outbreak, with 1,589 confirmed cases across 46 counties so far in 2026. Just five of the reported cases were vaccinated individuals.

State officials reiterated that the best protection against measles is to be fully vaccinated. The MMR vaccine — manufactured primarily by Merck (MRK) and GlaxoSmithKline (GSK) — provides 97% lifetime protection. 

While death from measles is rare, it does occur in one to three patients per 1,000 cases.

Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. blamed the COVID-19 pandemic for disrupting routine childhood vaccination.

"The multi-year global outbreak has caused many nations to lose their [measles] elimination status including, Armenia, Austria, Azerbaijan, Bolivia, Canada, Mexico, Spain, United Kingdom, and Uzbekistan," he posted on X. "We are working to close vaccination gaps and rebuild public trust."
